runtime.reason: Applicable public behavior is implemented and exercised by the named regression suites and shared fixtures. Rust unit tests are colocated with their implementation; complete tested modules are recorded as test evidence and exports/delegates as implementation evidence. HiveMind #251/#252 only changes the Python upstream client dispatcher; this consumer uses native single-dispatch transports (MCP delegates to the Node SDK), or caller-owned frame parsing in embedded C. No Python HiveMind bus dependency or slave-protocol reinjection exists here. Python now requires fixed upstream 1.1.9a1 and removes its identity-based suppression; equal independent native frames remain distinct. Reply claim metadata follows the Python string-ID contract, with first-seen ordering, case-sensitive fallback stages and legacy unstamped success. Invalid non-string stamps are ignored. Embedded C exposes bounded extraction and claim classification while its caller retains ordered IDs. A skill may now positively assert a claim via THALOVANT_CLAIMED_META_KEY ("thalovant_claimed") on its own speak event's data.meta; Reply::claimed checks only EVENT_SPEAK/EVENT_OVOS_UTTERANCE_SPEAK events for a literal true under that key, after the handled/ok/no-failure gate and before the pipeline-tier heuristic, so it can only turn a would-be false into true. A correlated non-speak event (e.g. ovos.utterance.handled) carrying the same meta shape is never scanned and cannot assert a claim. Anything but a literal true on a speak event is inert, and a reply that never sets the key is judged exactly as before.
